Jasper
JAS-per
noun
Greek iaspis (G2393), Hebrew yashpheh (H3471) — a translucent, often green or clear-crystalline quartz; first of the twelve foundation stones of the New Jerusalem (Rev 21:19) and the very stone that pictures the glory of God Himself appearing on the throne (Rev 4:3). The ancient iaspis was probably closer to what we today would call diamond or clear quartz — "clear as crystal" — not the opaque red-brown stone modern jewelers call jasper.

📖 Biblical Definition

Jasper is the first of the twelve precious stones laid as foundations beneath the city wall of New Jerusalem (Rev 21:19), and it is also the stone John saw when his vision lifted to the throne of God Himself: "He that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone" (Rev 4:3). The Holy Spirit chose this stone twice as a vehicle for the divine glory — clear, brilliant, refracting light without darkening it — because the God of glory is light, and in Him is no darkness at all (1 John 1:5). The city wall is built of jasper (Rev 21:18); the foundation begins with jasper; and the One on the throne shines as jasper. Old Testament jasper also appears in the high priest's breastplate (Exod 28:20; 39:13) — the last of the twelve stones representing the twelve tribes — and in Eden as one of the stones covering the anointed cherub before his fall (Ezek 28:13). The biblical-theological line runs: jasper covered Eden's covering cherub → jasper crowned the high priest's breastplate (representing the twelve tribes brought before God) → jasper lays the first foundation of the New Jerusalem (representing the twelve apostles and the twelve tribes united in the Lamb's city). The stone moves from a fallen anointed creature through the mediated approach of the priesthood to the unmediated dwelling of God with men. Jasper is the mineral testimony that God's glory is unbroken light — and that He has prepared a city for His people where that light needs no sun or moon, because the Lamb is the light thereof (Rev 21:23).

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A precious stone, the first foundation of the New Jerusalem and the appearance of Him who sits on the throne.

expand to see more

JASPER, noun. An opaque (the ancients said clear) impure quartz, of red, yellow, brown, green, or rarely blue color, sometimes striped or spotted. The biblical jasper of Rev 4:3 and 21:11 is described as "clear as crystal," suggesting the ancient stone was closer to diamond or clear quartz.

In Scripture, the first of the twelve foundation stones of the New Jerusalem (Rev 21:19); the eighth (KJV order, twelfth in Hebrew) stone of the high priest's breastplate (Exod 28:20); a covering of the anointed cherub in Eden (Ezek 28:13); the stone whose appearance signified the glory of God on the throne (Rev 4:3).

📖 Key Scripture

Revelation 21:19 — "And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones. The first foundation was jasper; the second, sapphire; the third, a chalcedony; the fourth, an emerald."

Revelation 4:3 — "And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone: and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald."

Revelation 21:11 — "Having the glory of God: and her light was like unto a stone most precious, even like a jasper stone, clear as crystal."

Ezekiel 28:13 — "Thou hast been in Eden the garden of God; every precious stone was thy covering, the sardius, topaz, and the diamond, the beryl, the onyx, and the jasper, the sapphire, the emerald, and the carbuncle, and gold."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Jasper is corrupted when stripped of its theological function and reduced to mere decoration, or when treated as a magical or healing crystal divorced from the Creator who made it.

expand to see more

On one side, modernist commentaries treat the foundation stones of Revelation 21 as nothing more than poetic adornment — pretty imagery, but signifying nothing in particular. This empties the text of meaning. The stones are chosen, ordered, and named by the Spirit; each carries weight tied to the high priest's breastplate, the temple, Eden, and the New Covenant people of God. To shrug at the names is to refuse what God Himself underlined twice in canon.

On the other side, New Age and crystal-healing spirituality co-opts biblical stones — jasper, sapphire, amethyst, emerald — and assigns them "vibrational frequencies," chakra alignments, or healing properties divorced from God. The Bible nowhere ascribes power to the stone itself; the stone is a vehicle for God's chosen revelation of His glory and His chosen ordering of His covenant people. Jasper does not heal you. The God whose throne shines like jasper heals — and that healing comes through the Lamb whose wounds purchased it, not through a polished rock.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek iaspis (G2393), Hebrew yashpheh (H3471) — a translucent precious stone whose ancient identification was closer to diamond/clear quartz than the modern opaque variety.

expand to see more

Greek iaspis (G2393) — jasper; in Revelation 4:3, 21:11, 21:18-19 a clear crystalline stone reflecting divine glory

Hebrew yashpheh (H3471) — jasper; the last stone of the high priest's breastplate (Exod 28:20) representing the twelfth tribe Benjamin

The ancient iaspis was probably a clear or diamond-like stone, NOT the modern opaque variegated jasper sold by jewelers today

Twice chosen for theophany contexts: God's appearance on the throne (Rev 4:3) and the foundation of the New Jerusalem (Rev 21:19)

Usage

"When John saw the throne, the One sitting upon it shone like jasper — the brilliance of unmediated divine glory."

"Jasper crowns the high priest's breastplate and founds the New Jerusalem: a stone bridging Old Covenant approach and New Covenant indwelling."

"Don't buy a jasper bracelet for healing; trust the God who chose jasper to picture the light of His face."
